subject.title: Feature Request: config:pre-apply hook for validating config changes

question: Should OpenClaw add a synchronous plugin-facing config-write veto API, and where must it sit relative to built-in config validation, SecretRef preflight, shared mutation helpers, and restart/reload scheduling?
rationale: This would create a public plugin/control-plane security boundary around persisted configuration writes, so code inspection can prove the gap but cannot choose the permanent fail-closed, redaction, timeout, actor-metadata, and API-compatibility contract.

options.title: Define guarded config-write veto
options.body: Approve a narrow public hook/API contract that runs after canonical validation/preflight and before persistence across all config mutation entry points, with typed rejection and regression tests.

options.title: Fold into broader preflight framework
options.body: Defer this specific hook until the broader plugin preflight/startup validation design chooses one validation framework and owner boundary.

options.title: Rely on built-in validation only
options.body: Close the API direction and keep external validators as opt-in skills or wrappers while continuing to harden core schema, SecretRef, and agent allowlist checks.

recommendation.title: Define guarded config-write veto
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow public hook/API contract that runs after canonical validation/preflight and before persistence across all config mutation entry points, with typed rejection and regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They already framed this exact issue as a config validation/mutation product-security decision and have recent adjacent config/security history.
